join_order.notes: Driver: tiny keyword slice yields ~few thousand mk rows
For each unique mv, scan mc offsets; require cn.country_code[company_id-1]==us_code; first match short-circuits
Dense PK on company_name; cn_cc[company_id-1] compared to resolved us_code (int16)
For each qualifying mv, iterate ci rows; collect person_ids
MIN aggregation: lex-compare each name to running min string_view

data_structures.k_id: int32 scalar (resolved from keyword.name dictionary lookup)
data_structures.movie_id_seen: flat_bitset(2528313) to dedupe movie_ids from mk slice
data_structures.thread_local_min: std::string per thread, merged at end

parallelism.notes: mk slice is tiny (~few thousand). Dedupe via bitset, then partition unique movie_ids across 12 threads. Each thread holds a local min string; final reduction picks overall min.

indexes.purpose: driver: locate mk rows for k_id

execution_notes: Step 1: dict-resolve '[us]' to int16 us_code from company_name/country_code.dict.off+.dict.dat.
Step 2: linear scan keyword.name varlen to find k_id where text == 'character-name-in-title'.
Step 3: lo=mk_k_off[k_id]; hi=mk_k_off[k_id+1]; for k in [lo,hi): mv=mk_movie_id[mk_k_row[k]]; mark in bitset.
Step 4: iterate set bits of bitset; for each mv test cn filter via mc offsets; if pass, expand ci offsets, update local min using std::string_view comparison on name varlen.
Step 5: reduce thread-local mins. Output single string.
